prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production enemy sprite for Depths, a dark stressful first-person pixel dungeon crawler. Silhouette-led restrained pixel art, large crisp clusters, at most three broad shades per material, warm upper-left highlights and dark cool shadows. Flat sparse surfaces, no individual fur, veins smaller than a large readable mark, no pores/grain/noise, no gradients/dithering/antialiasing, no glossy rendering, no ground shadow, background or text. Serious and unsettling, not cute/cartoon. Front-facing full-body transparent square canvas; keep all anatomy/equipment inside with generous 10% margins. Designed to reduce to a native128x128 sprite with max32 shared colours, bottom-centre scene origin (64,120). No scenery or UI. A pale dusty moth-thing as large as a dog, front-facing, four broad ragged wing lobes, narrow fur-less segmented body, long flexible proboscis curled forward beneath a tiny shadowed head. Two simple thin antennae; only a few large pale ivory/taupe wing patches, no tiny scales/ornamental eye spots or warm fuzzy fur. Drifting idle, wings partially mantled and detached from ground, no lantern or visible prey. Diseased unsettling cave life, clearly a moth silhouette, not a fairy/butterfly.
